suitability_reason: Section 86 inclusion of Social Security benefits received in 2016 despite a later (2020) repayment obligation; §86(d)(2)(A) reduces only by repayments made during the taxable year. Mechanical.

taxpayer.notes: Received Social Security disability benefits; eligibility ended in 2016 when she began a home business; repaying overpayment at $100/month since June 2020.

adjustments: included Social Security benefits of $13,024 in taxable income
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Benefits she must repay to SSA are like a loan and should be excluded from 2016 income.
conceded: Respondent conceded petitioner need not include nonemployee compensation of $1,983 in 2016 gross income

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner received Social Security benefits totaling $15,322 in 2016
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner received Social Security benefits totaling $15,322 in 2016.

findings_of_fact.fact: SSA concluded most or all 2016 benefits were not owed; repayment began June 2020 at $100/month (no repayment during 2016)
findings_of_fact.snippet: in June 2020 petitioner began repaying the excess benefits through monthly payments of $100 to the SSA.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2016 return reported Schedule C net profit of $82,395 and excluded the Social Security benefits
findings_of_fact.snippet: reporting net profits of $82,395 on Schedule C, Profit or Loss From Business, but she did not include the Social Security benefits

findings_of_fact.fact: Respondent determined $13,024 of Social Security benefits includible
findings_of_fact.snippet: determined that she was obliged to include Social Security benefits of $13,024 in taxable income for 2016.

issues.question: Are Social Security benefits received in 2016, which petitioner must repay to the SSA (repayment begun 2020), includible in her 2016 gross income?
issues.holding: Yes, to the extent provided by section 86; repayment in 2020 does not affect 2016 liability; respondent's section 86 computation sustained.
issues.computable_reason: Benefits received less repayments made in the same year (zero) run through §86 formula.

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Social Security inclusion sustained; Rule 155 reflects respondent's concession of $1,983 nonemployee compensation.

notes: Some facts stipulated. Dollar amounts rounded. Filing status not stated in opinion. Derived: 85% x $15,322 = $13,023.70 ~ $13,024 (consistent with 85% cap). Court did not consider effect of 86(d)(2)/1341 on later years.
